Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

(There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips and work out who owes whom."""
import sys

from .cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""Command-line interface: python3 -m kitty <command>."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from .errors import KittyError
from .ledger import Kitty, expense_json
from .money import fmt


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        # argparse exits with status 2 by default; kitty uses 1 for every error.
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        self.exit(1, f"{self.prog}: error: {message}\n")


def emit(value) -> None:
    print(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


def money_map(values: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {k: fmt(v) for k, v in values.items()}


# ----- command handlers -----


def cmd_init(args):
    kitty = Kitty.create(args.currency)
    print(f"Started a new kitty in {kitty.currency}")


def cmd_member_add(args):
    kitty = Kitty.load()
    name = kitty.add_member(args.name)
    kitty.save()
    print(f"Added {name}")


def cmd_member_remove(args):
    kitty = Kitty.load()
    name = kitty.remove_member(args.name)
    kitty.save()
    print(f"Removed {name}")


def cmd_member_list(args):
    emit(Kitty.load().members)


def cmd_expense_add(args):
    kitty = Kitty.load()
    expense = kitty.add_expense(
        args.payer,
        args.amount,
        " ".join(args.description),
        among=args.among,
        exact=args.exact,
        shares=args.shares,
        percent=args.percent,
        currency=args.currency,
        date=args.date,
        category=args.category,
    )
    kitty.save()
    print(expense.id)


def cmd_expense_list(args):
    emit([expense_json(e) for e in sorted(Kitty.load().expenses, key=lambda e: e.id)])


def cmd_expense_remove(args):
    kitty = Kitty.load()
    expense = kitty.remove_expense(args.id)
    kitty.save()
    print(f"Removed expense {expense.id} ({expense.description})")


def cmd_payment_add(args):
    kitty = Kitty.load()
    p = kitty.add_payment(args.sender, args.recipient, args.amount, args.currency, args.date)
    kitty.save()
    print(f"Recorded {p.sender} paying {p.recipient} {fmt(p.amount)} {p.currency}")


def cmd_rate_set(args):
    kitty = Kitty.load()
    currency, rate = kitty.set_rate(args.currency, args.rate)
    kitty.save()
    print(f"1 {currency} = {rate} {kitty.currency}")


def cmd_balances(args):
    emit(money_map(Kitty.load().balances()))


def cmd_settle(args):
    emit(
        [
            {"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": fmt(amount)}
            for debtor, creditor, amount in Kitty.load().settle()
        ]
    )


def cmd_history(args):
    emit(Kitty.load().history(args.name))


def cmd_report(args):
    emit({cat: money_map(people) for cat, people in Kitty.load().report().items()})


def cmd_export(args):
    count = Kitty.load().export_csv(args.file)
    print(f"Wrote {count} expense{'' if count == 1 else 's'} to {args.file}")


# ----- argument parsing -----


def add_group(sub, name, help_text):
    parser = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_text)
    return parser.add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True, metavar="action")


def build_parser() -> Parser:
    parser = Parser(prog="kitty", description="Track shared trip expenses and settle up.")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True, metavar="command")

    p = sub.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty in this directory")
    p.add_argument("currency", help="base currency, e.g. EUR")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_init)

    members = add_group(sub, "member", "manage the group")
    p = members.add_parser("add", help="add a member")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_add)
    p = members.add_parser("remove", help="remove a member")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_remove)
    p = members.add_parser("list", help="list members as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_list)

    expenses = add_group(sub, "expense", "record and review expenses")
    p = expenses.add_parser("add", help="record an expense and print its ID")
    p.add_argument("payer")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("description", nargs="+")
    split = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    split.add_argument("--among", metavar="A,B", help="split equally among these people only")
    split.add_argument("--exact", metavar="A=30,B=20", help="exact amount owed by each person")
    split.add_argument("--shares", metavar="A=2,B=1", help="split in proportion to shares")
    split.add_argument("--percent", metavar="A=60,B=40", help="split by percentages")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency paid in (default: base currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", help="YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)")
    p.add_argument("--category", help="category (default: other)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_add)
    p = expenses.add_parser("list", help="list expenses as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_list)
    p = expenses.add_parser("remove", help="remove an expense by ID")
    p.add_argument("id", type=int)
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_remove)

    payments = add_group(sub, "payment", "record repayments")
    p = payments.add_parser("add", help="record FROM paying TO back")
    p.add_argument("sender", metavar="FROM")
    p.add_argument("recipient", metavar="TO")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency paid in (default: base currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", help="YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_add)

    rates = add_group(sub, "rate", "manage exchange rates")
    p = rates.add_parser("set", help="set what one unit of CURRENCY is worth in the base currency")
    p.add_argument("currency")
    p.add_argument("rate")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_rate_set)

    p = sub.add_parser("balances", help="show each person's balance as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_balances)
    p = sub.add_parser("settle", help="suggest payments that settle all debts")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_settle)
    p = sub.add_parser("history", help="show everything that affected one person")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_history)
    p = sub.add_parser("report", help="show each person's spending per category")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_report)
    p = sub.add_parser("export", help="write expenses to a CSV file")
    p.add_argument("file")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_export)

    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        args.func(args)
    except KittyError as e:
        print(f"kitty: error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0

"""The kitty data model, its storage in kitty.json, and the calculations on it."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import re
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date as Date
from datetime import datetime
from decimal import Decimal

from .errors import KittyError
from .money import allocate, convert, fmt, parse_amount, parse_positive

FILENAME = "kitty.json"
FORMAT_VERSION = 1
DEFAULT_CATEGORY = "other"


@dataclass
class Expense:
    id: int
    seq: int
    date: str
    payer: str
    description: str
    amount: int  # cents, in `currency`
    currency: str
    rate: Decimal  # value of one unit of `currency` in the base currency, at entry time
    base_amount: int  # cents, base currency
    category: str
    shares: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)  # cents, base currency


@dataclass
class Payment:
    seq: int
    date: str
    sender: str
    recipient: str
    amount: int
    currency: str
    rate: Decimal
    base_amount: int


def normalize_currency(code: str) -> str:
    code = code.strip().upper()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{3}", code):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency code: {code!r} (expected three letters, like EUR)")
    return code


def parse_date(text: str | None) -> str:
    if text is None:
        return Date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(text.strip(), "%Y-%m-%d").date().isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (expected YYYY-MM-DD)") from None


def parse_pairs(text: str, option: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into [('A', '30'), ('B', '20')]."""
    pairs = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = item.rpartition("=")
        if not sep or not name.strip() or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"invalid {option} entry {item.strip()!r} (expected NAME=VALUE)")
        pairs.append((name.strip(), value.strip()))
    return pairs


class Kitty:
    def __init__(self, path: str, currency: str):
        self.path = path
        self.currency = currency
        self.members: list[str] = []
        self.rates: dict[str, Decimal] = {}
        self.expenses: list[Expense] = []
        self.payments: list[Payment] = []
        self.next_id = 1
        self.next_seq = 1

    # ----- storage -----

    @classmethod
    def create(cls, currency: str, path: str = FILENAME) -> "Kitty":
        if os.path.exists(path):
            raise KittyError(f"{path} already exists; remove it first to start a new kitty")
        kitty = cls(path, normalize_currency(currency))
        kitty.save()
        return kitty

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str = FILENAME) -> "Kitty":
        try:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = json.load(f)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            raise KittyError(f"no {path} here; run 'init CURRENCY' first") from None
        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
            raise KittyError(f"could not read {path}: {e}") from None
        try:
            kitty = cls(path, data["currency"])
            kitty.members = [str(m) for m in data["members"]]
            kitty.rates = {c: Decimal(str(r)) for c, r in data["rates"].items()}
            kitty.expenses = [
                Expense(
                    id=int(e["id"]),
                    seq=int(e["seq"]),
                    date=e["date"],
                    payer=e["payer"],
                    description=e["description"],
                    amount=parse_amount(e["amount"]),
                    currency=e["currency"],
                    rate=Decimal(str(e["rate"])),
                    base_amount=parse_amount(e["base_amount"]),
                    category=e["category"],
                    shares={n: parse_amount(s) for n, s in e["shares"].items()},
                )
                for e in data["expenses"]
            ]
            kitty.payments = [
                Payment(
                    seq=int(p["seq"]),
                    date=p["date"],
                    sender=p["from"],
                    recipient=p["to"],
                    amount=parse_amount(p["amount"]),
                    currency=p["currency"],
                    rate=Decimal(str(p["rate"])),
                    base_amount=parse_amount(p["base_amount"]),
                )
                for p in data["payments"]
            ]
            kitty.next_id = int(data["next_id"])
            kitty.next_seq = int(data["next_seq"])
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError, ArithmeticError, KittyError):
            raise KittyError(f"{path} is damaged or not a kitty file") from None
        return kitty

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "version": FORMAT_VERSION,
            "currency": self.currency,
            "members": self.members,
            "rates": {c: str(r) for c, r in self.rates.items()},
            "expenses": [
                {
                    "id": e.id,
                    "seq": e.seq,
                    "date": e.date,
                    "payer": e.payer,
                    "description": e.description,
                    "amount": fmt(e.amount),
                    "currency": e.currency,
                    "rate": str(e.rate),
                    "base_amount": fmt(e.base_amount),
                    "category": e.category,
                    "shares": {n: fmt(s) for n, s in e.shares.items()},
                }
                for e in self.expenses
            ],
            "payments": [
                {
                    "seq": p.seq,
                    "date": p.date,
                    "from": p.sender,
                    "to": p.recipient,
                    "amount": fmt(p.amount),
                    "currency": p.currency,
                    "rate": str(p.rate),
                    "base_amount": fmt(p.base_amount),
                }
                for p in self.payments
            ],
            "next_id": self.next_id,
            "next_seq": self.next_seq,
        }

    def save(self) -> None:
        # Write to a temporary file and rename, so a crash never leaves a half-written kitty.
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
        try:
            fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    json.dump(self.to_dict(), f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                    f.write("\n")
                os.replace(tmp, self.path)
            except BaseException:
                os.unlink(tmp)
                raise
        except OSError as e:
            raise KittyError(f"could not write {self.path}: {e}") from None

    # ----- members -----

    def resolve(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Find a member by name, ignoring case."""
        wanted = name.strip().casefold()
        for member in self.members:
            if member.casefold() == wanted:
                return member
        raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name.strip()!r}")

    def resolve_distinct(self, names: list[str], option: str) -> list[str]:
        resolved = [self.resolve(n) for n in names]
        for i, name in enumerate(resolved):
            if name in resolved[:i]:
                raise KittyError(f"{name} is listed more than once in {option}")
        return resolved

    def add_member(self, name: str) -> str:
        name = name.strip()
        if not name:
            raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
        if any(c in name for c in ",="):
            raise KittyError(f"member name cannot contain ',' or '=': {name!r}")
        if any(m.casefold() == name.casefold() for m in self.members):
            raise KittyError(f"{name} is already a member")
        self.members.append(name)
        return name

    def remove_member(self, name: str) -> str:
        name = self.resolve(name)
        used = any(e.payer == name or name in e.shares for e in self.expenses) or any(
            name in (p.sender, p.recipient) for p in self.payments
        )
        if used:
            raise KittyError(
                f"{name} appears in recorded expenses or payments; remove those first"
            )
        self.members.remove(name)
        return name

    # ----- currencies -----

    def set_rate(self, currency: str, rate: str) -> tuple[str, Decimal]:
        currency = normalize_currency(currency)
        if currency == self.currency:
            raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
        value = parse_positive(rate, "rate")
        self.rates[currency] = value
        return currency, value

    def rate_for(self, currency: str | None) -> tuple[str, Decimal]:
        if currency is None:
            return self.currency, Decimal(1)
        currency = normalize_currency(currency)
        if currency == self.currency:
            return currency, Decimal(1)
        if currency not in self.rates:
            raise KittyError(
                f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one with 'rate set {currency} RATE'"
            )
        return currency, self.rates[currency]

    def _to_base(self, amount: int, currency: str, rate: Decimal) -> int:
        base = convert(amount, rate)
        if base <= 0:
            raise KittyError(f"{fmt(amount)} {currency} is less than 0.01 {self.currency}")
        return base

    # ----- expenses and payments -----

    def add_expense(
        self,
        payer: str,
        amount: str,
        description: str,
        among: str | None = None,
        exact: str | None = None,
        shares: str | None = None,
        percent: str | None = None,
        currency: str | None = None,
        date: str | None = None,
        category: str | None = None,
    ) -> Expense:
        if sum(opt is not None for opt in (among, exact, shares, percent)) > 1:
            raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares and --percent")
        payer = self.resolve(payer)
        cents = parse_amount(amount)
        currency, rate = self.rate_for(currency)
        base = self._to_base(cents, currency, rate)
        description = description.strip()
        if not description:
            raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
        category = (category if category is not None else DEFAULT_CATEGORY).strip().lower()
        if not category:
            raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")
        date = parse_date(date)

        weights: list[Decimal | int]
        if exact is not None:
            pairs = parse_pairs(exact, "--exact")
            names = self.resolve_distinct([n for n, _ in pairs], "--exact")
            weights = [parse_amount(v, f"amount for {n}") for n, (_, v) in zip(names, pairs)]
            if sum(weights) != cents:
                raise KittyError(
                    f"--exact amounts add up to {fmt(sum(weights))}, "
                    f"but the expense is {fmt(cents)}"
                )
        elif shares is not None:
            pairs = parse_pairs(shares, "--shares")
            names = self.resolve_distinct([n for n, _ in pairs], "--shares")
            weights = [parse_positive(v, f"share for {n}") for n, (_, v) in zip(names, pairs)]
        elif percent is not None:
            pairs = parse_pairs(percent, "--percent")
            names = self.resolve_distinct([n for n, _ in pairs], "--percent")
            weights = [parse_positive(v, f"percentage for {n}") for n, (_, v) in zip(names, pairs)]
            if sum(weights) != 100:
                raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {sum(weights)}, not 100")
        else:
            if among is not None:
                listed = [n for n in among.split(",") if n.strip()]
                if not listed:
                    raise KittyError("--among needs at least one name")
                names = self.resolve_distinct(listed, "--among")
            else:
                if not self.members:
                    raise KittyError("there are no members yet; add some with 'member add NAME'")
                names = list(self.members)
            weights = [1] * len(names)

        # Present shares in membership order, whatever order they were typed in.
        split = dict(zip(names, allocate(base, weights)))
        split = {m: split[m] for m in self.members if split.get(m)}

        expense = Expense(
            id=self.next_id,
            seq=self.next_seq,
            date=date,
            payer=payer,
            description=description,
            amount=cents,
            currency=currency,
            rate=rate,
            base_amount=base,
            category=category,
            shares=split,
        )
        self.expenses.append(expense)
        self.next_id += 1
        self.next_seq += 1
        return expense

    def remove_expense(self, expense_id: int) -> Expense:
        for expense in self.expenses:
            if expense.id == expense_id:
                self.expenses.remove(expense)
                return expense
        raise KittyError(f"no expense with ID {expense_id}")

    def add_payment(
        self,
        sender: str,
        recipient: str,
        amount: str,
        currency: str | None = None,
        date: str | None = None,
    ) -> Payment:
        sender = self.resolve(sender)
        recipient = self.resolve(recipient)
        if sender == recipient:
            raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
        cents = parse_amount(amount)
        currency, rate = self.rate_for(currency)
        payment = Payment(
            seq=self.next_seq,
            date=parse_date(date),
            sender=sender,
            recipient=recipient,
            amount=cents,
            currency=currency,
            rate=rate,
            base_amount=self._to_base(cents, currency, rate),
        )
        self.payments.append(payment)
        self.next_seq += 1
        return payment

    # ----- reports -----

    def balances(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        result = {m: 0 for m in self.members}
        for e in self.expenses:
            result[e.payer] += e.base_amount
            for name, share in e.shares.items():
                result[name] -= share
        for p in self.payments:
            result[p.sender] += p.base_amount
            result[p.recipient] -= p.base_amount
        return result

    def settle(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, int]]:
        """Suggest transfers that bring every balance to zero (at most n-1 of them)."""
        order = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(self.members)}
        owed = {m: b for m, b in self.balances().items() if b > 0}
        owing = {m: -b for m, b in self.balances().items() if b < 0}
        transfers = []
        while owed and owing:
            # Largest debtor pays largest creditor; ties broken by membership order.
            creditor = min(owed, key=lambda m: (-owed[m], order[m]))
            debtor = min(owing, key=lambda m: (-owing[m], order[m]))
            amount = min(owed[creditor], owing[debtor])
            transfers.append((debtor, creditor, amount))
            for pool, name in ((owed, creditor), (owing, debtor)):
                pool[name] -= amount
                if not pool[name]:
                    del pool[name]
        return transfers

    def history(self, name: str) -> list[dict]:
        name = self.resolve(name)
        events = []
        for e in self.expenses:
            if e.payer == name or name in e.shares:
                paid = e.base_amount if e.payer == name else 0
                events.append((e.date, e.seq, e.description, paid - e.shares.get(name, 0)))
        for p in self.payments:
            if p.sender == name:
                events.append((p.date, p.seq, f"Payment to {p.recipient}", p.base_amount))
            elif p.recipient == name:
                events.append((p.date, p.seq, f"Payment from {p.sender}", -p.base_amount))
        events.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[0], ev[1]))
        balance = 0
        rows = []
        for when, _, description, change in events:
            balance += change
            rows.append(
                {
                    "date": when,
                    "description": description,
                    "change": fmt(change),
                    "balance": fmt(balance),
                }
            )
        return rows

    def report(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
        totals: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
        for e in self.expenses:
            category = totals.setdefault(e.category, {})
            for name, share in e.shares.items():
                category[name] = category.get(name, 0) + share
        return {
            cat: {m: totals[cat][m] for m in self.members if m in totals[cat]}
            for cat in sorted(totals)
        }

    def export_csv(self, path: str) -> int:
        columns = [
            "id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"
        ]
        try:
            with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                writer = csv.writer(f)
                writer.writerow(columns)
                for e in sorted(self.expenses, key=lambda e: e.id):
                    writer.writerow(
                        [
                            e.id,
                            e.date,
                            e.payer,
                            e.description,
                            fmt(e.amount),
                            e.currency,
                            e.category,
                            fmt(e.base_amount),
                        ]
                    )
        except OSError as e:
            raise KittyError(f"could not write {path}: {e}") from None
        return len(self.expenses)


def expense_json(e: Expense) -> dict:
    return {
        "id": e.id,
        "date": e.date,
        "payer": e.payer,
        "description": e.description,
        "amount": fmt(e.amount),
        "currency": e.currency,
        "base_amount": fmt(e.base_amount),
        "category": e.category,
        "shares": {n: fmt(s) for n, s in e.shares.items()},
    }

"""Money helpers. All amounts are handled internally as integer cents."""

from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

from .errors import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def parse_decimal(text: str, what: str) -> Decimal:
    try:
        value = Decimal(str(text).strip())
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}") from None
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_positive(text: str, what: str) -> Decimal:
    value = parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be greater than zero: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_amount(text: str, what: str = "amount") -> int:
    """Parse a positive amount with at most two decimal places into cents."""
    value = parse_positive(text, what)
    try:
        if value != value.quantize(CENT):
            raise KittyError(f"{what} can have at most two decimal places: {text!r}")
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} is too large: {text!r}") from None
    return int(value * 100)


def fmt(cents: int) -> str:
    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
    cents = abs(cents)
    return f"{sign}{cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"


def convert(cents: int, rate: Decimal) -> int:
    """Convert cents of a foreign currency to cents of the base currency, halves rounding up."""
    return int((Decimal(cents) * rate).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def allocate(total: int, weights: list[Decimal | int]) -> list[int]:
    """Split total cents in proportion to weights so the parts sum exactly to total.

    Each part is its exact portion rounded down to the cent; the cents left over
    then go one each to the parts in the order given.
    """
    weights = [Decimal(w) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(weights)
    # Decimal's // is exact integer division, so the floors involve no rounding.
    parts = [int(Decimal(total) * w // weight_sum) for w in weights]
    for i in range(total - sum(parts)):
        parts[i] += 1
    return parts

def normalize_currency(code: str) -> str:

    pairs = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = item.rpartition("=")
        if not sep or not name.strip() or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"invalid {option} entry {item.strip()!r} (expected NAME=VALUE)")
        pairs.append((name.strip(), value.strip()))
    return pairs

        self.expenses: list[Expense] = []
        self.payments: list[Payment] = []
        self.next_id = 1
        self.next_seq = 1

    @classmethod
    def create(cls, currency: str, path: str = FILENAME) -> "Kitty":

            raise KittyError(f"{path} already exists; remove it first to start a new kitty")
        kitty = cls(path, normalize_currency(currency))

        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:

            kitty.expenses = [

                    seq=int(e["seq"]),
                    date=e["date"],
                    payer=e["payer"],
                    description=e["description"],
                    amount=parse_amount(e["amount"]),
                    currency=e["currency"],
                    rate=Decimal(str(e["rate"])),
                    base_amount=parse_amount(e["base_amount"]),

                    date=p["date"],
                    sender=p["from"],
                    recipient=p["to"],
                    amount=parse_amount(p["amount"]),
                    currency=p["currency"],
                    rate=Decimal(str(p["rate"])),

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "version": FORMAT_VERSION,
            "currency": self.currency,
            "members": self.members,
            "rates": {c: str(r) for c, r in self.rates.items()},
            "expenses": [
                {
                    "id": e.id,
                    "seq": e.seq,
                    "date": e.date,
                    "payer": e.payer,
                    "description": e.description,
                    "amount": fmt(e.amount),
                    "currency": e.currency,
                    "rate": str(e.rate),
                    "base_amount": fmt(e.base_amount),
                    "category": e.category,
                    "shares": {n: fmt(s) for n, s in e.shares.items()},
                }
                for e in self.expenses
            ],
            "payments": [
                {
                    "seq": p.seq,
                    "date": p.date,
                    "from": p.sender,
                    "to": p.recipient,
                    "amount": fmt(p.amount),
                    "currency": p.currency,
                    "rate": str(p.rate),
                    "base_amount": fmt(p.base_amount),
                }
                for p in self.payments
            ],
            "next_id": self.next_id,
            "next_seq": self.next_seq,
        }

    def save(self) -> None:
        # Write to a temporary file and rename, so a crash never leaves a half-written kitty.
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
        try:
            fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    json.dump(self.to_dict(), f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                    f.write("\n")

    # ----- members -----

    def resolve(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Find a member by name, ignoring case."""
        wanted = name.strip().casefold()
        for member in self.members:
            if member.casefold() == wanted:
                return member
        raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name.strip()!r}")

    def resolve_distinct(self, names: list[str], option: str) -> list[str]:
        resolved = [self.resolve(n) for n in names]
        for i, name in enumerate(resolved):
            if name in resolved[:i]:
                raise KittyError(f"{name} is listed more than once in {option}")
        return resolved

    def add_member(self, name: str) -> str:
        name = name.strip()
        if not name:
            raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
        if any(c in name for c in ",="):
            raise KittyError(f"member name cannot contain ',' or '=': {name!r}")
        if any(m.casefold() == name.casefold() for m in self.members):
            raise KittyError(f"{name} is already a member")
        self.members.append(name)
        return name

    def remove_member(self, name: str) -> str:
        name = self.resolve(name)
        used = any(e.payer == name or name in e.shares for e in self.expenses) or any(
            name in (p.sender, p.recipient) for p in self.payments

        if used:

        self.members.remove(name)
        return name

    def set_rate(self, currency: str, rate: str) -> tuple[str, Decimal]:
        currency = normalize_currency(currency)
        if currency == self.currency:
            raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
        value = parse_positive(rate, "rate")
        self.rates[currency] = value
        return currency, value

    def rate_for(self, currency: str | None) -> tuple[str, Decimal]:
        if currency is None:
            return self.currency, Decimal(1)
        currency = normalize_currency(currency)
        if currency == self.currency:
            return currency, Decimal(1)
        if currency not in self.rates:
            raise KittyError(
                f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one with 'rate set {currency} RATE'"
            )
        return currency, self.rates[currency]

    def _to_base(self, amount: int, currency: str, rate: Decimal) -> int:
        base = convert(amount, rate)
        if base <= 0:
            raise KittyError(f"{fmt(amount)} {currency} is less than 0.01 {self.currency}")
        return base

    # ----- expenses and payments -----

    def add_expense(
        self,
        payer: str,
        amount: str,
        description: str,
        among: str | None = None,
        exact: str | None = None,
        shares: str | None = None,
        percent: str | None = None,
        currency: str | None = None,
        date: str | None = None,
        category: str | None = None,
    ) -> Expense:
        if sum(opt is not None for opt in (among, exact, shares, percent)) > 1:
            raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares and --percent")
        payer = self.resolve(payer)
        cents = parse_amount(amount)
        currency, rate = self.rate_for(currency)
        base = self._to_base(cents, currency, rate)
        description = description.strip()
        if not description:
            raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
        category = (category if category is not None else DEFAULT_CATEGORY).strip().lower()
        if not category:
            raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")
        date = parse_date(date)

        weights: list[Decimal | int]
        if exact is not None:
            pairs = parse_pairs(exact, "--exact")
            names = self.resolve_distinct([n for n, _ in pairs], "--exact")
            weights = [parse_amount(v, f"amount for {n}") for n, (_, v) in zip(names, pairs)]
            if sum(weights) != cents:
                raise KittyError(
                    f"--exact amounts add up to {fmt(sum(weights))}, "
                    f"but the expense is {fmt(cents)}"
                )
        elif shares is not None:
            pairs = parse_pairs(shares, "--shares")
            names = self.resolve_distinct([n for n, _ in pairs], "--shares")
            weights = [parse_positive(v, f"share for {n}") for n, (_, v) in zip(names, pairs)]
        elif percent is not None:
            pairs = parse_pairs(percent, "--percent")
            names = self.resolve_distinct([n for n, _ in pairs], "--percent")
            weights = [parse_positive(v, f"percentage for {n}") for n, (_, v) in zip(names, pairs)]
            if sum(weights) != 100:
                raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {sum(weights)}, not 100")
        else:
            if among is not None:
                listed = [n for n in among.split(",") if n.strip()]
                if not listed:
                    raise KittyError("--among needs at least one name")
                names = self.resolve_distinct(listed, "--among")
            else:
                if not self.members:
                    raise KittyError("there are no members yet; add some with 'member add NAME'")
                names = list(self.members)
            weights = [1] * len(names)

        split = dict(zip(names, allocate(base, weights)))
        split = {m: split[m] for m in self.members if split.get(m)}

            id=self.next_id,
            seq=self.next_seq,
            date=date,
            payer=payer,
            description=description,
            amount=cents,
            currency=currency,
            rate=rate,
            base_amount=base,
            category=category,

        self.next_id += 1
        self.next_seq += 1
        return expense

    def remove_expense(self, expense_id: int) -> Expense:
        for expense in self.expenses:
            if expense.id == expense_id:
                self.expenses.remove(expense)
                return expense
        raise KittyError(f"no expense with ID {expense_id}")

    def add_payment(
        self,
        sender: str,
        recipient: str,
        amount: str,
        currency: str | None = None,
        date: str | None = None,
    ) -> Payment:
        sender = self.resolve(sender)
        recipient = self.resolve(recipient)
        if sender == recipient:
            raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
        cents = parse_amount(amount)
        currency, rate = self.rate_for(currency)
        payment = Payment(
            seq=self.next_seq,
            date=parse_date(date),
            sender=sender,
            recipient=recipient,
            amount=cents,
            currency=currency,
            rate=rate,
            base_amount=self._to_base(cents, currency, rate),
        )

        self.next_seq += 1
        return payment

    def balances(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        result = {m: 0 for m in self.members}
        for e in self.expenses:
            result[e.payer] += e.base_amount
            for name, share in e.shares.items():
                result[name] -= share
        for p in self.payments:
            result[p.sender] += p.base_amount
            result[p.recipient] -= p.base_amount
        return result

    def settle(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, int]]:
        """Suggest transfers that bring every balance to zero (at most n-1 of them)."""
        order = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(self.members)}
        owed = {m: b for m, b in self.balances().items() if b > 0}
        owing = {m: -b for m, b in self.balances().items() if b < 0}
        transfers = []
        while owed and owing:
            # Largest debtor pays largest creditor; ties broken by membership order.
            creditor = min(owed, key=lambda m: (-owed[m], order[m]))
            debtor = min(owing, key=lambda m: (-owing[m], order[m]))
            amount = min(owed[creditor], owing[debtor])
            transfers.append((debtor, creditor, amount))
            for pool, name in ((owed, creditor), (owing, debtor)):
                pool[name] -= amount
                if not pool[name]:
                    del pool[name]
        return transfers

    def history(self, name: str) -> list[dict]:
        name = self.resolve(name)
        events = []
        for e in self.expenses:
            if e.payer == name or name in e.shares:
                paid = e.base_amount if e.payer == name else 0
                events.append((e.date, e.seq, e.description, paid - e.shares.get(name, 0)))
        for p in self.payments:
            if p.sender == name:
                events.append((p.date, p.seq, f"Payment to {p.recipient}", p.base_amount))
            elif p.recipient == name:
                events.append((p.date, p.seq, f"Payment from {p.sender}", -p.base_amount))
        events.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[0], ev[1]))
        balance = 0
        rows = []
        for when, _, description, change in events:
            balance += change
            rows.append(
                {
                    "date": when,
                    "description": description,
                    "change": fmt(change),
                    "balance": fmt(balance),

            )
        return rows

    def report(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
        totals: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
        for e in self.expenses:
            category = totals.setdefault(e.category, {})
            for name, share in e.shares.items():
                category[name] = category.get(name, 0) + share
        return {
            cat: {m: totals[cat][m] for m in self.members if m in totals[cat]}
            for cat in sorted(totals)
        }

    def export_csv(self, path: str) -> int:
        columns = [
            "id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"
        ]
        try:
            with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:

                writer.writerow(columns)

                            e.payer,
                            e.description,
                            fmt(e.amount),

                            e.category,
                            fmt(e.base_amount),
                        ]
                    )
        except OSError as e:
            raise KittyError(f"could not write {path}: {e}") from None
        return len(self.expenses)


def expense_json(e: Expense) -> dict:
    return {

        "description": e.description,
        "amount": fmt(e.amount),

"""Money helpers. All amounts are handled internally as integer cents."""

from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

from .errors import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def parse_decimal(text: str, what: str) -> Decimal:
    try:
        value = Decimal(str(text).strip())
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}") from None
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_positive(text: str, what: str) -> Decimal:
    value = parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be greater than zero: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_amount(text: str, what: str = "amount") -> int:
    """Parse a positive amount with at most two decimal places into cents."""
    value = parse_positive(text, what)
    try:
        if value != value.quantize(CENT):
            raise KittyError(f"{what} can have at most two decimal places: {text!r}")
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} is too large: {text!r}") from None
    return int(value * 100)


def fmt(cents: int) -> str:
    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
    cents = abs(cents)
    return f"{sign}{cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"


def convert(cents: int, rate: Decimal) -> int:
    """Convert cents of a foreign currency to cents of the base currency, halves rounding up."""
    return int((Decimal(cents) * rate).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def allocate(total: int, weights: list[Decimal | int]) -> list[int]:
    """Split total cents in proportion to weights so the parts sum exactly to total.

    Each part is its exact portion rounded down to the cent; the cents left over
    then go one each to the parts in the order given.
    """
    weights = [Decimal(w) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(weights)
    # Decimal's // is exact integer division, so the floors involve no rounding.
    parts = [int(Decimal(total) * w // weight_sum) for w in weights]
    for i in range(total - sum(parts)):
        parts[i] += 1
    return parts

I've added both features. All 25 tests pass: the 20 that were already there and 5 new ones for these features.

**`expense edit ID`**
- It changes only the options you give and keeps the expense's ID and its place in `history`.
- If the amount or currency changes without a split option, it's split equally among the same people as before. A split option on its own re-splits the current amount, and `--exact` has to add up to that amount.
- A different currency is converted at its current rate. If `--currency` names the currency the expense already has, the rate recorded with the expense is kept. That fits how rates are fixed when an expense is entered.
- Edits are all-or-nothing: if any part is invalid (unknown person, bad date, missing rate, `--exact` that doesn't add up), nothing is saved.
- On success it prints `Updated expense 1 (Cab)`, the same style as `expense remove`.

**`balances --in CUR` / `settle --in CUR`**
- Amounts are converted at the current rate and rounded to the cent, with halves rounding up, as the existing conversions do. The JSON is the same as before.
- A currency with no rate gives the usual "no exchange rate for …" error. The base currency gives the usual amounts.
- `settle` still works out who pays whom in the base currency and converts each transfer afterwards. Because each one is rounded separately, the converted transfers can be a cent off the converted balances.

**Decisions you might want to change:**
- `expense edit` with no options is an error ("nothing to change") rather than doing nothing silently.
- `--description` takes a single argument, so descriptions with spaces need quotes, e.g. `--description "Dinner out"`. `expense add` takes the words unquoted.
- If a tiny expense left someone with a 0.00 share, they weren't stored in its split. An equal re-split on edit therefore won't include them; use `--among` to add them back.

To support editing, I moved the split calculation in `kitty/ledger.py` out of `add_expense` into a helper that both commands use. `expense add` behaves exactly as before. The conversion for `--in` is a new `convert_from_base` function in `kitty/money.py`.
